purpose: Canonical evidence for cryptographic and digital-money precursors to Bitcoin.

records.title: Diffie and Hellman publish New Directions in Cryptography
records.summary: Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman published the foundational public-key cryptography paper that introduced a way to establish secure communications without first sharing a secret key.
records.significance: Public-key cryptography and digital signatures are fundamental building blocks beneath secure digital money and cryptocurrency.

records.title: RSA public-key cryptosystem is introduced
records.summary: Rivest, Shamir and Adleman produced the MIT technical report describing the RSA public-key cryptosystem; the journal version followed in 1978.
records.significance: RSA became one of the foundational systems for public-key encryption and digital signatures.

sources.title: MIT — A Method for Obtaining Digital Signatures and Public-key Cryptosystems

records.title: David Chaum proposes blind signatures for untraceable digital payments
records.summary: David Chaum presented Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments at CRYPTO '82, describing cryptographic techniques that could support private electronic cash.
records.significance: Chaum's work is one of the clearest direct technical ancestors of privacy-preserving digital money.

records.title: The Crypto Anarchist Manifesto circulates
records.summary: Timothy May later dated The Crypto Anarchist Manifesto to mid-1988 and said it was distributed at Crypto '88; he posted it electronically to the Cypherpunks list in November 1992.
records.significance: The manifesto articulated the privacy, censorship-resistance and cryptographic-sovereignty ideas that shaped the cypherpunk movement.

records.title: DigiCash is founded
records.summary: David Chaum founded DigiCash to commercialize privacy-preserving cryptographic electronic cash.
records.significance: DigiCash was the most important commercial pre-Bitcoin effort to deploy cryptographic cash through banks and payment networks.

records.title: Cypherpunks mailing list begins
records.summary: Eric Hughes sent the welcome message that established the Cypherpunks mailing-list infrastructure on toad.com.
records.significance: The mailing list became a central forum for privacy, cryptography, anonymous digital cash and ideas that directly preceded Bitcoin.

records.title: A Cypherpunk's Manifesto is published
records.summary: Eric Hughes published A Cypherpunk's Manifesto to the Cypherpunks mailing list.
records.significance: It became the defining concise statement of the movement's belief that privacy should be defended through cryptography and code.

records.title: DigiCash records an early eCash payment over computer networks
records.summary: Chaum's eCash history records a first electronic-cash payment over computer networks on 27 May 1994, with broader trials following.
records.significance: It demonstrated working cryptographic digital cash more than a decade before Bitcoin.

records.title: Adam Back proposes Hashcash
records.summary: Adam Back originally proposed Hashcash in May 1997 as a proof-of-work mechanism for resisting spam and denial-of-service abuse.
records.significance: Bitcoin explicitly builds on Hashcash-style proof of work, making it a direct technical ancestor of Bitcoin mining.

sources.title: Hashcash — A Denial of Service Counter-Measure

records.title: Wei Dai publishes b-money
records.summary: Wei Dai published b-money in November 1998, describing protocols for money and contracts among untraceable digital pseudonyms.
records.significance: Satoshi cited b-money in the Bitcoin whitepaper, making it a direct conceptual predecessor.

records.title: DigiCash enters bankruptcy
records.summary: DigiCash entered bankruptcy after failing to achieve broad commercial adoption.
records.significance: Its failure illustrates the centralization and adoption problems that earlier cryptographic-cash systems had not solved.

records.title: Hal Finney announces reusable proof of work (RPOW)
records.summary: Hal Finney announced RPOW, a server system that exchanged Hashcash proofs for transferable reusable proof-of-work tokens.
records.significance: RPOW was a sophisticated pre-Bitcoin experiment in scarce, transferable proof-of-work-based digital value.

records.title: Nick Szabo publishes Bit Gold proposal
records.summary: The surviving primary Bit Gold publication is Nick Szabo's 29 December 2005 post describing scarce digital objects created through proof of work and timestamping.
records.significance: Bit Gold is a major conceptual ancestor of Bitcoin's digital scarcity and proof-of-work design.
records.notes: Many secondary timelines date the concept to 1998; the archive uses the surviving primary publication date rather than repeating that unsourced date.
